Metadata.title: Orrery
Metadata.description: Self-hosted control panel for your GitHub repositories

Setup.title: Set up Orrery
Setup.tokenIntro: Enter the setup token printed in the container logs. It proves you operate this server.
Setup.createIntro: Next, create the GitHub App that signs you in and reads your repositories. You will go to GitHub and come back here.
Setup.createPermissions: The app is read-only: metadata, contents, issues, pull requests, actions and organization members.
Setup.doneBody: Install it on the accounts and organizations whose repositories you want to see. Then sign in with GitHub in this browser: the first sign-in becomes the instance admin.

Auth.title: Sign in to Orrery
Auth.intro: Orrery shows what GitHub lets you see. Sign in with the GitHub account you use for your repositories.

Shell.emptyBody: A repository shows up here once it has a .hub.yml file on its default branch and the GitHub App can read it.
Shell.issuesShowingLast: Showing the last valid version until they are fixed.
Shell.issuesNeverValid: Nothing can be shown until they are fixed.
Shell.noWidgets: This page has no widgets yet.

Secrets.title: Secrets of {project}
Secrets.intro: Secrets are write-only: once saved, a value is never shown again. Each one is only ever sent to the hosts it is bound to.
Secrets.errorTitle: The secret could not be saved
Secrets.formHelp: Saving a name that already exists replaces its value and hosts.
Secrets.name: Name

ProjectSettings.title: Settings of {project}
ProjectSettings.errorTitle: The change could not be made
ProjectSettings.hostsIntro: Without any entry, sources may reach every public host the instance allows. With entries, they may only reach the hosts listed here. A project can narrow what is allowed, never open more.
ProjectSettings.hostsEmpty: No restriction: every public host is allowed.
ProjectSettings.secretsBody: Write-only values bound to the hosts they may be sent to.
ProjectSettings.reindexBody: Read the configuration file again from GitHub now, instead of waiting for the next push or poll.

Widgets.errorTitle: This widget could not load its data
Widgets.crashed: This widget could not be drawn.

Admin.title: Instance settings
Admin.errorTitle: The change could not be made
Admin.signInIntro: Level 1 of the access policy. Entries are org:'<'login>, team:'<'org>/'<'slug> or user:'<'login>. GitHub's own permissions still apply: the hub only narrows.
Admin.signInEmpty: The list is empty: nobody can sign in except admins.
Admin.rulesIntro: Level 2. Hide a project from everyone, or restrict it to a user or a team. Hiding wins over everything.
Admin.rulesEmpty: No rule: GitHub decides who sees each project.
Admin.hostsIntro: Hosts, suffixes, addresses or CIDR ranges that sources may reach even though they are private. Only an admin can open one.
Admin.hostsEmpty: None: private addresses are refused everywhere.
Admin.adminsIntro: Admins manage everything on this page. ORRERY_ADMINS adds admins again at every start.
Admin.keysIntro: After adding a new active key to ORRERY_ENCRYPTION_KEYS (keep the old ones after it), re-encrypt everything with it.
Admin.keysStatus: Active key: {active}. Still on another key: {pending, number}.
Admin.keysUnavailable: The encryption keys could not be read.
Admin.auditIntro: The 50 latest entries. Entries are kept for a year and cannot be changed.

Tokens.title: Agent tokens
Tokens.intro: Tokens let an AI agent read what you can read, and nothing more. They are read-only, expire, and stop working if you lose access.
Tokens.createdBody: Copy it now: it is shown once and cannot be recovered.
Tokens.errorTitle: The token could not be created
Tokens.formHelp: Lifetime: {days} days by default, {max} at most.
Tokens.name: Label

Settings.title: Settings
Settings.themeBody: Remembered in this browser only. System follows your device.
